name: What should be included in a new home construction contract?

mainEntity.name: What items should be clearly listed in a custom home construction contract so nothing is missed?
mainEntity.text: What items should be clearly listed in a custom home construction contract so nothing is missed?

acceptedAnswer.text: A strong custom home construction contract should make the scope, budget, and responsibilities clear before work begins. At minimum, it should spell out the exact scope of work, allowances, payment schedule, change order process, permit responsibilities, timeline assumptions, warranty coverage, exclusions, and cleanup duties. It should also identify who is responsible for selections, inspections, and subcontractor coordination. In luxury or custom projects, the contract should define finish levels carefully so there is no confusion about what quality is included. If the proposal relies on estimates, those estimates should be easy to track and update. The best contracts reduce ambiguity and make decisions visible early, which is critical when a project involves many trades and material choices. If any part of the scope is vague, ask for a written clarification before signing.
acceptedAnswer.description: A good construction contract should list the scope of work, allowances, schedule, payment terms, change order process, warranty terms, exclusions, permit responsibilities, and who handles site cleanup and inspections. The contract should also define finish levels and what happens if design changes are requested.
